title: fix(macos): retain queued input across native reconnect
body:
Closes #192642

## What Problem This Solves

Offline queued input can disappear when the macOS app reconnects to the same Gateway and replaces its embedded dashboard document.

## User Impact

The dashboard keeps its page state when only the native socket reconnects. Actual endpoint, configured credential, TLS and browser-account changes still isolate documents; no configuration or migration is required.

**Live native verification completed:** the exact candidate app passes the real-Gateway offline-queue recovery flow below. The exact-head native proof is complete; this PR is being evaluated for landing. No deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Socket-owned startup credentials retire before the next authenticated connection arrives. Treating that temporary projection as a new document owner discards the WebView containing the queue. The fix separates document identity from socket authority across the existing lifetime decisions and refreshes the retained document's future-load credentials, without weakening native challenge checks or changing global auth equality.

## Evidence

Tested source: `2430b2ec27cf81f90b9beba2c4928bb5d132d4da`.

- Extended the existing real-native-auth/WebKit regression to cover retirement both before and after reconnect. The unchanged production base fails the retirement-first case on controller/WebView retention and native challenge availability (3 failures, 3.72 seconds); the existing opposite ordering passes.
- The fixed candidate passes **33 native tests across four suites in the retained disposable macOS guest**, including both retirement orders, retained draft/sessionStorage, fresh challenge scopes, startup credentials after manual reload, route/credential replacement, and untrusted-source rejection (14.40 seconds). These use simulated Gateway sockets; the separate live real-Gateway outage proof is below.
- Native build, pinned SwiftFormat and diff checks pass. Pinned SwiftLint reports inherited file-length errors in `DashboardManager.swift` (base 1513, candidate 1514) and unchanged `GatewayConnection.swift` (1505); no rule was suppressed.
- Completed pinned local ClawSweeper review of this exact committed candidate: no actionable correctness or security findings. At review time, it identified the live candidate-app recovery proof as missing; that separate proof is now completed below.

No production deployment is included.

## Live candidate-app outage proof (2026-11-04)

**The actual fixed app now passes the offline queue/reconnect flow in the retained disposable macOS guest.**

Tested pair: native app `2026.10.10 (2610001090)`, full commit `2430b2ec27cf81f90b9beba2c4928bb5d132d4da` (also verified in its native About panel); real isolated Gateway and embedded UI `f95b9464cf64178675498ae7823fc374a3c40cf2`. The Gateway contains the separate auth-copy fix, not a queue workaround. Native and Gateway commits are intentionally recorded separately.

Reproduction replay through the native saved-Gateway window, without diagnostic UI instrumentation:

1. Build/package the exact native candidate with the repository's supported packager. Strict deep signature verification and matching bundled-runtime provenance pass; independently verify the same signature and commit after copying it into the guest.
2. Connect a saved profile to the same task-owned, authenticated foreground Gateway. Send `Reply with exactly: QUEUE_FIXED_READY_1104` through the native composer and verify the exact real-model answer before creating an outage.
3. With that session idle, terminate only the recorded fixture launcher, collect exit 0, and verify its listener is closed. Submit `Reply with exactly: QUEUE_FIXED_OFFLINE_1104` through the native send button. The row remains visibly marked `Waiting for reconnect`, with `1 queued` in the sidebar.
4. Restart the same fixture state, token and pairing. Initial embedded native-authorization retries are visible; native authentication succeeds at 10:14:52 UTC and embedded authentication at 10:15:00 UTC. The queued item stays in custody through those retries, then automatically becomes one user turn and the exact assistant answer. No manual resend or replacement fresh prompt is used.
5. Native Cmd+R reload retains both recovered turns. After graceful fixture shutdown, a read-only scan of all **60** retained transcript events, decoding all **6** compressed payloads, finds exactly one user and one assistant event for each new marker; the queued marker is not duplicated.

Before screenshots below are the earlier diagnosed native failure, native `d48be80a63791215ff337596cf93f0cb5b80a233` plus the same Gateway/UI `f95b9464cf64178675498ae7823fc374a3c40cf2` with a clearly labeled diagnostic overlay. They are not mislabeled as a same-commit native base-app run. The deterministic unchanged-base red regression is the separate native WebKit test documented above. Fixed screenshots are the uninstrumented actual candidate.

Scope and cleanup: this live arm exercises the saved-Gateway native window; the primary-window and both lease-observation orders are covered by the existing native regression suites, not claimed as additional live outage runs. No exhaustive race/load, release-upgrade or channel qualification is implied. The disposable Gateway exited 0 with listener closed, the retained guest shut down normally and was verified stopped, the shared desktop lease is free, and production config and host app identity remain unchanged. That proof run performed no deployment, ready-for-review transition or merge. The disposable VM, restore cache, runtimes, fixture state and generated builds were subsequently retired to macOS Trash by the coordinator; source and compact proof remain.
